text_blocks.snippet: Common scams active in Central Illinois include fake local repair service impersonations, fraudulent state agency text messages, and door-to-door home repair cons.
snippet_highlighted_words: fake local repair service impersonations, fraudulent state agency text messages, and door-to-door home repair cons

list.snippet: Imposter Garage Repair: Scammers set up fake online ads and numbers pretending to be real local businesses (like Bloomington’s The Door Doctor or Peoria providers), vastly overcharging or damaging equipment.
Fake DMV & Secretary of State Texts: Fraudulent text messages claim vehicle registration or driving privileges are suspended, or promise fake fuel rebates, urging users to click phishing links.
Storm Chasing Contractors: Door-to-door workers demand upfront cash for urgent roof or home repairs after bad weather, then fail to finish the work or disappear.
Deed and Property Fraud: Criminals falsify documents or pose as owners to illegally sell vacant land or properties in counties like Sangamon.
Verify phone numbers: Look up local businesses independently rather than clicking the top sponsored search result.
Ignore official texts: State offices like the Illinois Secretary of State never text residents regarding fee payments or license suspensions.
Never pay cash upfront: Do not sign immediate contracts or pay full amounts before home repair work is completed and checked.
Report suspicious activity: Contact the Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois or the Illinois Attorney General if you suspect fraud.
